Before, signing the form did nothing and the pull was still blocked. Second: a staff member at one company could file a permission record naming a client belonging to a DIFFERENT company. That is now refused.

notes: COMPLIANCE REVIEW REQUIRED (CLAUDE.md §7): consent capture, credit-pull type. Logged as the marker you asked for, with no advice attached.

OWNER DECISION LOGGED, NOT RE-RAISED. The new file's header records Chris's 2026-08-19 call as owner-set, names the earlier decision it reverses (src/handlers/contract-signed.mjs:41-48, 'two writers for one permission is how a revocation stops biting'), and then treats that old reasoning as the spec for the guards rather than as an objection. contract-signed.mjs itself is untouched.

HOW A WITHDRAWAL KEEPS BITING — the rule, in plain words: a signature can only grant permission that did not already exist when it was signed. If the client took the permission back at or after the moment they signed, the withdrawal wins, forever. Signing a NEW form later still works normally, because that is a new signature with a later date. Enforced in one SQL statement against the database's own clock, never against the web server's.

HOW A REPLAY IS STOPPED: one signed paper produces at most one permission record. The check is on client_consents.document_id, the same column the row is written with, so there is no second key to keep in step. A record already pointing at that paper stops it whether it is live OR revoked — which is what makes revocation keep biting on the ordinary replay path too. I also wrote down out loud in the file that this does NOT protect against two dispatches of the same event running at the exact same instant; nothing in this repo does that today, and if it ever does the fix is a unique index, not a lock.

WHAT COUNTS AS THE SOFT-PULL FORM. I checked the real values instead of guessing. db/seed/007_contract_templates.sql lines 62-64 give the SOFT-PULL-CONSENT template kind='authorization' and subtype='soft_pull_consent'; src/config/offers.mjs:42 is where the template key 'SOFT-PULL-CONSENT' comes from; src/contracts/send.mjs:167 copies kind and subtype onto every contract. I gate on the (kind, subtype) PAIR, NOT the template key. Reason: template_key is just a label an org can set to anything (src/contracts/templates.mjs), so gating on it would let a contract that merely borrowed the name unlock a credit pull. Side effect worth knowing: an authorization whose subtype was left blank records nothing and the pull stays blocked. That is the safe direction and it is visible, because the pull is refused out loud.

A TEST I WROTE FOUND A REAL BUG IN MY OWN CODE, and I fixed it rather than deleting the test. merge_values is free-form JSON. The form says 'this permission lasts N days'. My first version turned that value into text before checking its shape — and in JavaScript an empty list turns into an empty string, so a list would have read as 'no time limit at all' and written a PERMANENT permission off a form that granted 90 days. Now anything that is not plain text or a number is refused, digits only, and a number too big to be a real date is refused too. If the form names a time limit we cannot read, nothing is written at all — I never fall back to 'never expires'.

HOW LONG THE PERMISSION LASTS. The seeded form says the permission lasts a set number of days (007:75, a required blank the send screen refuses to skip, filled with 90 on the normal path per src/config/offers.mjs:130). I honour that: the record expires that many days after they signed. If a form names no time limit at all, the record does not expire, because nothing said it would. I did not invent a default.

WHO THE RECORD IS ATTRIBUTED TO. The signing link is anonymous (an HMAC over the contract id, src/contracts/sign.mjs:64-71), so there is no portal account to point at and granted_by_account_id is a real foreign key. The record is therefore attributed to the staff member who SENT the form for signature, with the client's own signed name in granted_name. That is exactly the meaning migration 099's header assigns to a staff-attributed consent. If nobody sent it, nothing is written.

KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than smoothed over, and it is in the file header. The client reads the CONTRACT wording; the stored record holds the approved server wording 'soft-pull-v1'. Those are not the same paragraph. I did it that way because the brief and api/consent/capture.mjs both require the words to come from the server, and the server's version claims nothing the contract does not, and the record points at the exact paper they signed. Reconciling the two wordings is a decision, not a code change.

THE MULTI-TENANT HOLE, and what it actually did. api/consent/capture.mjs's ownsClient() returned true for ANY staff member with no check at all, while the comment above it claimed it was copied from api/finance/soft-pull.mjs and 'answered identically'. It did not. Both finance endpoints run `SELECT 1 FROM clients WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2`; this one ran nothing. Because a permission record is what unlocks a credit pull, the loose endpoint was a way around the strict one. It now runs the same query, word for word, and I rewrote the false comment to say what happened.

BOTH AWAITS ARE IN, and there is a test for each separately. Making that check async means a missed `await` returns a Promise, and a Promise is always truthy, so `!promise` is false and the check silently switches OFF instead of failing loudly. One missed await would disable it on exactly one method while the other method's test still passed. I test GET and POST separately, plus revoke, plus a check that the org used is the session's, plus a check that nothing is read or written before the check runs.

I also added a source-text check that api/consent/capture.mjs and api/finance/soft-pull.mjs still contain the identical org query, in the same idiom as the existing test in that file that compares the two role lists.

NO TEST WAS WEAKENED, SKIPPED OR DELETED anywhere. The 39 existing tests in src/http/consent-capture.test.mjs all still run and all still pass; I only taught the fake database to answer the new org query, with a switch (`owns: false`) the new refusal tests flip.

Handler tests live beside the handler in this repo (every file in src/handlers has a matching <name>.test.mjs), so I created src/handlers/contract-consent.test.mjs. I did not edit any existing test file other than the one in my list.
